title: Safe areas, notches and screen insets
when: Fixed headers or bottom bars are hidden behind the notch, the status bar or the home indicator, or full height layouts jump when the browser toolbar moves.
prompt:
Goal: Layout that draws edge to edge but keeps text and buttons inside the safe area in portrait and landscape.
Steps:
1. Add viewport-fit=cover to the viewport meta; without it env() insets are always 0.
2. Declare tokens: :root { --inset-top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px); --inset-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px); --inset-left: env(safe-area-inset-left, 0px); --inset-right: env(safe-area-inset-right, 0px); }.
3. Header: padding-top: calc(12px + var(--inset-top)); bottom bar: padding-bottom: max(8px, var(--inset-bottom)).
4. In landscape pad the sides with --inset-left and --inset-right so content clears the notch.
5. Full height screens: height: 100vh first, then height: 100dvh on the next line for browsers that know it.
6. In a Capacitor shell call StatusBar.setOverlaysWebView({ overlay: true }) only when the page draws under the status bar, and match StatusBar.setStyle to the header color.
7. Backgrounds may extend under insets; tappable things may not.
Quality bar:
- No button sits in the home indicator strip.
- Rotation does not hide content behind the notch.
Pitfalls:
- Hard coding 44px or 20px for the status bar.
- Using 100vh alone, which leaves content under the toolbar.
- Insets on body only, while fixed bars ignore them.
Verify:
- [ ] The viewport meta has viewport-fit=cover.
- [ ] Fixed header and bottom bar use the inset tokens.
- [ ] Checked in portrait and both landscape sides.
Output: the viewport meta in index.html and the inset rules in app.css.

examples.input: minha barra de baixo fica atrás do risquinho do celular
examples.output: viewport-fit=cover, inset tokens with env(), bottom bar padding max(8px, inset), 100dvh
